summary:

title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
summary:
In an announcement on Wednesday, the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company's "Starmind" initiative. With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space, including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full "constellation" of AI satellites.

title: Nothing offers a full look at its AI earbuds and charging case
summary:
Nothing is showing off a much more detailed look at its upcoming AI earbuds ahead of their December 8th release. The Ear Note buds can record your calls, while their charging case can record, transcribe, and summarize your conversations.
Like the Ear 3, the Ear Note's microphone-equipped case comes with a "Talk" button that you can use to record your own voice. There's also a new "Record" button that can record and transcribe your conversations. In a post on X, Nothing CEO Carl Pei says the button will allow you to record calls through the earbuds, and meetings through the case as a "first step toward a hardware context layer for AI."

title: Has vibe coding made open source the new normal for synths?
summary:
The emergence of powerful vibe-coding agents and tools like Reverse Engineer Anything has caused chaos in the music gear world, leaving companies scrambling to figure out how to respond. While some, like Roland, have remained silent for now, others have embraced the modding community. title: CrowdStrike’s Zscaler deal aims to give security teams a single kill switch for rogue AI agents
summary:

summary:

title: Nearly half of surveyed engineers and leaders say the AI agents that write their code also review it
summary:
As AI coding tools generate more code, review has become a constraint on how fast that code ships. But only 26% of respondents to a new survey say they are very confident they understand AI-generated changes as thoroughly as human-written ones.

summary:

title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
summary:
Tidal is officially banning AI-generated music on December 9th. As a result of this change, Tidal will delete around 29 million AI-generated songs and reject an estimated 80,000 to 85,000 tracks per day, according to Tidal music lead Robert Andersen.
The move comes just months after Tidal began labeling and demonetizing tracks identified as 100 percent AI-generated. In a post on X, Andersen says Tidal needed to take a more "drastic" measure, as AI music made up 43 percent of the tracks distributed to the platform in the last 90 days. summary:
